description?: string): Promise<{ backupId: string; metadata: BackupMetadata }> {\n    const backupId = `backup_${Date.now()}_${crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex')}`;\n    let totalRecords = 0;\n    let tableCount = 0;\n    const tableStats: any[] = [];\n\n    // Define table mappings for each category - using actual table names from database\n    const categoryTables: Record<string, string[]> = {\n      procurement: ['purchase_requisitions', 'requisition_items', 'approval_history', 'rfq_requests', \n                   'rfq_responses', 'purchase_orders', 'purchase_order_items',\n                   'goods_receipts', 'goods_receipt_items'],\n      jobs: ['jobs', 'job_materials', 'cutting_plans', 'cut_sequences'],\n      finance: ['quotes', 'quote_history', 'quote_views'],\n      audit: [] // Skip audit tables for now as they may have issues\n    };\n\n    // Process each category without a transaction to avoid rollback issues\n    for (const category of categories) {\n      const tables = categoryTables[category] || [];\n      \n      for (const tableName of tables) {\n        try {\n          // Get all records from the table using raw SQL\n          const result = await db.execute(sql.raw(`SELECT * FROM ${tableName}`));\n          const records = result.rows;\n          \n          if (records.length > 0) {\n            tableCount++;\n            totalRecords += records.length;\n            tableStats.push({ table: tableName, count: records.length });\n            \n            // Store each record in backup_data in batches\n            const batchSize = 100;\n            for (let i = 0; i < records.length; i += batchSize) {\n              const batch = records.slice(i, i + batchSize);\n              const insertValues = batch.map(record => ({\n                backupId,\n                tableName,\n                recordData: record,\n                originalRecordId: record.id || null\n              }));\n              \n              try {\n                await db.insert(backupData).values(insertValues);\n              } catch (batchError) {\n                console.error(`Error inserting batch for table ${tableName}:`, batchError);\n              }\n            }\n          }\n        } catch (error) {\n          console.error(`Error backing up table ${tableName}:`, error);\n          // Continue with other tables even if one fails\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Create backup metadata record\n    const [metadata] = await db.insert(backupMetadata).values({\n      backupId,\n      backupName: description || `Backup ${new Date().toLocaleString()}`,\n      description,\n      backupType: 'manual',\n      categories: categories,\n      tableCount,\n      recordCount: totalRecords,\n      backupSize: totalRecords * 1000, // Rough estimate\n      status: 'active',\n      createdBy: userId\n    }).returning();\n\n    return { backupId, metadata };\n  }\n\n  async listBackups(): Promise<BackupMetadata[]> {\n    return await db\n      .select()\n      .from(backupMetadata)\n      .where(eq(backupMetadata.status, 'active'))\n      .orderBy(desc(backupMetadata.createdAt));\n  }\n\n  async getBackupDetails(backupId: string): Promise<{ metadata: BackupMetadata; tableStats: any[] }> {\n    const [metadata] = await db\n      .select()\n      .from(backupMetadata)\n      .where(eq(backupMetadata.backupId, backupId));\n\n    // Get table statistics\n    const stats = await db\n      .select({\n        tableName: backupData.tableName,\n        count: sql<number>`COUNT(*)::int`\n      })\n      .from(backupData)\n      .where(eq(backupData.backupId, backupId))\n      .groupBy(backupData.tableName);\n\n    return { metadata, tableStats: stats };\n  }\n\n  async restoreBackup(backupId: string, userId: number): Promise<{ success: boolean; message: string }> {\n    try {\n      // Get backup metadata\n      const [metadata] = await db\n        .select()\n        .from(backupMetadata)\n        .where(eq(backupMetadata.backupId, backupId));\n\n      if (!metadata) {\n        return { success: false, message: 'Backup not found' };\n      }\n\n      // Get all backup data\n      const backupRecords = await db\n        .select()\n        .from(backupData)\n        .where(eq(backupData.backupId, backupId));\n\n      // Group records by table\n      const recordsByTable: Record<string, any[]> = {};\n      for (const record of backupRecords) {\n        if (!recordsByTable[record.tableName]) {\n          recordsByTable[record.tableName] = [];\n        }\n        recordsByTable[record.tableName].push(record.recordData);\n      }\n\n      // Clear existing data and restore from backup\n      await db.transaction(async (tx) => {\n        // First clear the target tables\n        for (const tableName of Object.keys(recordsByTable)) {\n          try {\n            await tx.execute(sql.raw(`TRUNCATE TABLE ${tableName} CASCADE`));\n          } catch (error) {\n            console.error(`Error clearing table ${tableName}:`, error);\n          }\n        }\n\n        // Then restore the data\n        for (const [tableName, records] of Object.entries(recordsByTable)) {\n          for (const record of records) {\n            try {\n              // Build dynamic insert query\n              const columns = Object.keys(record).join(', ');\n              const values = Object.values(record);\n              const placeholders = values.map((_, i) => `$${i + 1}`).join(', ');\n              \n              await tx.execute(sql.raw(`INSERT INTO ${tableName} (${columns}) VALUES (${placeholders})`, values));\n            } catch (error) {\n              console.error(`Error restoring to table ${tableName}:`, error);\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      });\n\n      // Update metadata\n      await db\n        .update(backupMetadata)\n        .set({ restoredAt: new Date() })\n        .where(eq(backupMetadata.backupId, backupId));\n\n      return { success: true, message: 'Backup restored successfully' };\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error('Restore error:', error);\n      return { success: false, message: 'Failed to restore backup' };\n    }\n  }\n\n  async deleteBackup(backupId: string): Promise<void> {\n    // Delete backup data\n    await getNextSequenceNumber(sequenceType: string): Promise<string> {\n    // Get or create sequence\n    let [sequence] = await db\n      .select()\n      .from(numberingSequences)\n      .where(eq(numberingSequences.sequenceType, sequenceType));\n\n    if (!sequence) {\n      // Create new sequence with defaults\n      const prefix = sequenceType + '-';\n      [sequence] = await db\n        .insert(numberingSequences)\n        .values({\n          sequenceType,\n          currentNumber: 0,\n          prefix,\n          includeYear: false,\n          padLength: 5,\n          startingNumber: 1\n        })\n        .returning();\n    }\n\n    // Increment and get next number\n    const nextNumber = sequence.currentNumber + 1;\n    \n    // Update the sequence\n    await db\n      .update(numberingSequences)\n      .set({ \n        currentNumber: nextNumber,\n        updatedAt: new Date()\n      })\n      .where(eq(numberingSequences.sequenceType, sequenceType));\n\n    // Format the number\n    const paddedNumber = String(nextNumber).padStart(sequence.padLength, '0');\n    \n    if (sequence.includeYear) {\n      const year = new Date().getFullYear();\n      return `${sequence.prefix}${year}-${paddedNumber}`;\n    } else {\n      return `${sequence.prefix}${paddedNumber}`;\n    }\n  }\n\n  async updateNumberingSequence(sequenceType: string, updates: Date, endDate: Date): Promise<{ availability: number; performance: number; quality: number; oee: number }> {\n    const metrics = await this.getProductionMetrics(startDate, endDate);\n    \n    if (metrics.length === 0) {\n      return { availability: 0, performance: 0, quality: 0, oee: 0 };\n    }\n    \n    const totals = metrics.reduce((acc, metric) => ({\n      availability: acc.availability + (Number(metric.availability) || 0),\n      performance: acc.performance + (Number(metric.performance) || 0),\n      quality: acc.quality + (Number(metric.quality) || 0),\n      oee: inspections.filter(i => i.status === 'failed').length;\n    const conditional = inspections.filter(i => i.status === 'conditional').length;\n    const passRate = total > 0 ? now = new Date();\n      let startDate = new Date();\n      \n      // Set date range based on period\n      switch (period) {\n        case 'week':\n          startDate.setDate(now.getDate() - 7);\n          break;\n        case 'month':\n          startDate.setMonth(now.getMonth() - 1);\n          break;\n        case 'quarter':\n          startDate.setMonth(now.getMonth() - 3);\n          break;\n        case 'year':\n          startDate.setFullYear(now.getFullYear() - 1);\n          break;\n        case 'all':\n        default:\n          startDate = new Date('2020-01-01');\n          break;\n      }\n\n      // Build job query with date filter\n      const jobQuery = db.select().from(jobs);\n      const conditions = [];\n      if (jobId) {\n        conditions.push(eq(jobs.id, jobId));\n      }\n      if (period !== 'all') {\n        conditions.push(gte(jobs.createdAt, startDate));\n      }\n      if (conditions.length > 0) {\n        jobQuery.where(and(...conditions));\n      }\n      const jobsData = await jobQuery;\n\n      // Get purchase orders for actual material costs\n      const purchaseOrdersData = await db.select()\n        .from(purchaseOrders)\n        .leftJoin(purchaseOrderItems, eq(purchaseOrders.id, purchaseOrderItems.purchaseOrderId));\n\n      // Get time entries for actual labor costs - simplified query\n      const whereConditions = [isNotNull(timeEntries.clockOut)];\n      if (jobId) {\n        whereConditions.push(eq(timeEntries.jobId, jobId));\n      }\n      \n      const timeEntriesRaw = await db\n        .select()\n        .from(timeEntries)\n        .where(and(...whereConditions));\n      \n      // Process time entries data\n      const timeEntriesData = timeEntriesRaw.map(entry => ({\n        jobId: entry.jobId,\n        totalHours: entry.totalHours || 0,\n        employeeId: entry.userId,\n        hourlyRate: entry.hourlyRate || 50\n      }));\n\n      // Calculate actual labor costs by job\n      const laborCostByJob = new Map<number, number>();\n      timeEntriesData.forEach(entry => {\n        if (entry.jobId) {\n          const currentCost = laborCostByJob.get(entry.jobId) || 0;\n          const hourlyRate = entry.hourlyRate || 50; // Default $50/hour if no rate set\n          const laborCost = (entry.totalHours || 0) * hourlyRate;\n          laborCostByJob.set(entry.jobId, currentCost + laborCost);\n        }\n      });\n\n      // Calculate actual material costs by job from purchase orders\n      const materialCostByJob = new Map<number, number>();\n      purchaseOrdersData.forEach(po => {\n        if (po.purchase_orders?.jobId && po.purchase_order_items) {\n          const jobId = po.purchase_orders.jobId;\n          const currentCost = materialCostByJob.get(jobId) || 0;\n          const itemCost = parseFloat(po.purchase_order_items.totalPrice || '0');\n          materialCostByJob.set(jobId, currentCost + itemCost);\n        }\n      });\n\n      // Calculate overview metrics\n      let totalEstimatedCost = 0;\n      let totalActualCost = 0;\n      let overBudgetJobs = 0;\n      let underBudgetJobs = 0;\n\n      const cost from real sources\n        const actualLaborCost = laborCostByJob.get(job.id) || 0;\n        const actualMaterialCost = materialCostByJob.get(job.id) || parseFloat(job.materialCost || '0');\n apiRequest(`/api/${apiEndpoint}`, \"POST\", contactData);\n    },\n    onSuccess: () => {\n      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [apiEndpoint, entityId] });\n      queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: [apiEndpoint, entityId] });\n      setIsAddDialogOpen(false);\n      addForm.reset();\n      toast({ \n        title: \"Contact added successfully\",\n        description: autoMarkAsPrimary && contacts.length === 0 ? \"Contact marked as primary\" : undefined\n      });\n    },\n    onError: (error) => {\n      toast({ title: \"Error adding contact\", description: error.message, variant: \"destructive\" });\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Update contact mutation\n  const updateContactMutation = useMutation({\n    mutationFn: async (contactData: any) => {\n      return apiRequest(`/api/${apiEndpoint}/${contactData.id}`, \"PATCH\", contactData);\n    },\n    onSuccess: () => {\n      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [apiEndpoint, entityId] });\n      queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: [apiEndpoint, entityId] });\n      setIsEditDialogOpen(false);\n      setEditingContact(null);\n      editForm.reset();\n      toast({ title: \"Contact updated successfully\" });\n    },\n    onError: (error) => {\n      toast({ title: \"Error updating contact\", description: error.message, variant: \"destructive\" });\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Delete contact via ${apiEndpoint}`);\n      \n      // Make the delete request\n      const response = await fetch(`/api/${apiEndpoint}/${contactId}`, {\n        method: 'DELETE',\n        headers: {\n          'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n        },\n      });\n      \n      if (!response.ok) {\n        throw new Error(`Failed to delete contact: ${response.status}`);\n      }\n      \n ${entityId}`);\n      \n      // Multiple refresh strategies to ensure UI updates\n      await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [apiEndpoint, entityId] });\n      await queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: [apiEndpoint, entityId] });\n      \n      toast({ title: \"Contact deleted successfully\" });\n    },\n    onError: (error) => {\n      console.error(`Delete </Button>\n            <Button\n              variant={viewMode === \"list\" ? \"default\" : \"ghost\"}\n              size=\"sm\"\n              onClick={() => setViewMode(\"list\")}\n PrinterConfig {\n  ip: string;\n  port: number;\n  dpi: 203 | 300 | 600;\n  labelWidth: number; // in mm\n  labelHeight: number; // in mm\n}\n\nexport class ZebraPrinterService {\n  private config: const lineHeight = this.mmToDots(7);\n\n    // Build ZPL command\n    const zpl = failed: 0, errors: [] as string[] };\n    const total = this.queue.length;\n\n    try {\n      for (let i = 0; i < this.queue.length; i++) {\n        const label = this.queue[i];\n        \n        if (onProgress) {\n          onProgress(i + 1, total);\n        }\n\n        const success = await this.printer.printLabel(label);\n        \n        if (success) {\n          results.success++;\n (Basic)\n```typescript\nconst overheads = directCosts × (overheadPercentage / 100);\n```\n\n## Enhanced Overhead Calculation Framework\n\n### 1. Operational Expenses (OPEX) - Monthly/Annual\n- **Workshop Rent**: $8,000/month × 12 = $96,000/year\n- **Utilities**: Power, gas, water - $2,500/month × 12 = $30,000/year\n- **Insurance**: Public liability, equipment, workers comp - $15,000/year\n- **Administration**: Office rent, accounting, software licenses - $36,000/year\n- **Staff Overhead**: Non-billable staff costs - $120,000/year\n\n**Total Annual OPEX**: $297,000\n\n### 2. Capital Expenses (CAPEX) - Depreciation\n- **Workshop Equipment**: $500,000 over 10 years = $50,000/year\n- **Vehicles**: $150,000 over 5 years = $30,000/year\n- **Tools & Machinery**: $100,000 over 7 years = $14,286/year\n\n**Total Annual CAPEX Depreciation**: $94,286\n\n### 3. Dynamic Overhead Rate Calculation\n```typescript\nconst annualRevenue = 1500000; // $1.5M annual revenue target\nconst totalOverheads = annualOPEX + annualCAPEX; // $391,286\nconst overheadRate = (totalOverheads / annualRevenue) * 100; // 26.1%\n```\n\n### 4. Project-Specific Overhead Adjustments\n- **Small Projects (<$50k)**: Base rate + 5% (higher admin burden)\n- **Large Projects (>$200k)**: Base rate - 3% (economies of scale)\n- **Site Work**: Base rate + 8% (travel, accommodation, site costs)\n- **Workshop Only**: Base rate - 2% (no travel/site costs)\n\n## Proposed Input Form for Overhead Management\n\n### Monthly OPEX Tracking:\n- Workshop 'text-red-600 bg-red-50';\n  if (grossProfitMargin < 30) return 'text-orange-600 bg-orange-50';\n  return 'text-green-600 Multi-Tiered Rate Structure (STRUMIS/Tekla Standard)\nFortune 500 companies use sophisticated rate hierarchies:\n\n```\nLabor Rate Hierarchy:\n├── Company Base Rates\n│   ├── Trade Classifications (Welder, Fitter, Rigger)\n│   ├── Skill Levels (Apprentice, Journeyman, Master)\n│   └── Certification Premiums (AWS, ASME, API)\n├── Project-Specific Rates\n│   ├── Client Contract Rates\n│   ├── Location Adjustments\n│   └── Shift Differentials\n└── Real-Time Cost Tracking\n    ├── Actual vs. Budgeted Rates\n    ├── Overtime Multipliers\n    └── Productivity Factors\n```\n\n### 2. Dynamic Rate Calculation Model\n\n**Industry Best Practice Formula:**\n```\nEffective Labor Rate = Base Rate × Location Factor × Skill Multiplier × Certification Premium × Shift Differential × Productivity Factor\n```\n\n**Example from STRUMIS:**\n- Base Rate: $45/hour (Journeyman Welder)\n- Location Factor: 1.15 (Urban area)\n- Skill Multiplier: 1.10 (5+ years experience)\n- Certification Premium: 1.08 (AWS D1.1)\n- Shift Differential: 1.00 (Day shift)\n- Productivity Factor: 0.95 (Historical performance)\n- **Effective Rate: $56.21/hour**\n\n### 3. Geographic Rate Management (SAP/Oracle)\n- **Regional Rate Tables**: Different rates by state/region\n- **Union vs. Non-Union Rates**: Separate rate structures\n- **Prevailing Wage Integration**: Automatic Davis-Bacon compliance\n- **Cost of Living Adjustments**: Annual COLA updates\n\n#### C. Real-Time Rate Application (Tekla/STRUMIS)\n- **Automatic Rate Selection**: Based on worker qualifications\n- **Rate Override Controls**: With audit trail\n- **Rate Escalation**: Automatic increases based on contracts\n- **Multi-Currency Support**: For international projects\n\n### 4. Integration with Estimation\n\n**Fortune 500 Estimation Workflow:**\n\n1. **Rate Selection During Estimation**\n   - System suggests rates based on:\n     - Project location\n     - Required certifications\n     - Historical project data\n     - Current market conditions\n\n2. **Rate Variance Analysis**\n   - Compare estimated vs. actual rates\n   - Identify cost overruns early\n   - Adjust future estimates based on actuals\n\n3. **Burden Rate Calculation**\n   - Automatically includes:\n     - Payroll taxes (FICA, Medicare, FUTA, SUTA)\n     - Workers' compensation\n     - General liability insurance\n     - Benefits (health, retirement, vacation)\n     - Small tools and consumables\n\n### 5. (CORRECT - Industry Standard)\n\n### Method: Margin on Direct Costs Before Overheads\n```typescript\nconst directCosts = materials + labor + equipment + consumables + coatings;\nconst overheads = directCosts × (overheadPercentage / 100);\nconst margin = directCosts × (marginPercentage / 100);  // KEY: On direct costs only\nconst total = directCosts + overheads + margin;\n```\n\n### Example with $30,000 Direct Costs:\n- **Direct Costs**: $30,000 (materials, labor, equipment, consumables, coatings)\n- **Overheads (20%)**: $30,000 × 0.20 = $6,000\n- **Margin (20%)**: $30,000 × 0.20 = $6,000 (calculated on direct costs)\n- **Total Price**: $30,000 + $6,000 + $6,000 = $42,000\n\n**Effective Markup**: $12,000 ÷ $30,000 = 40% markup on direct costs\n**Gross Profit Margin**: $12,000 ÷ $42,000 = 28.6% of revenue\n\n## Alternative Methods (Why They're Wrong for Steel Fabrication)\n\n### Method 2: Margin on Total Costs (INCORRECT - Double Compounds)\n```typescript\n// WRONG APPROACH\nconst directCosts = materials + labor + equipment + consumables + coatings;\nconst overheads = directCosts × (overheadPercentage / 100);\nconst subtotal = directCosts + overheads;\nconst margin = subtotal × (marginPercentage / 100);  // ERROR: Compounds margin\nconst total = subtotal + margin;\n```\n\n### Same Example with WRONG Method:\n- **Direct Costs**: $30,000\n- **Overheads (20%)**: $6,000\n- **Subtotal**: $36,000\n- **Margin (20%)**: $36,000 × 0.20 = $7,200 (inflated by overhead inclusion)\n- **Total Price**: $36,000 + $7,200 = $43,200\n\n**Problem**: Price inflated by $1,200 (2.9% higher) - makes bids uncompetitive\n\n### Method 3: Percentage Markup (Alternative - Valid but Less Common)\n```typescript\n// Alternative valid approach\nconst directCosts = materials + labor + equipment + consumables + coatings;\nconst markup = directCosts × (markupPercentage / 100);\nconst total = directCosts + markup;\n// Then overheads are included within the markup calculation\n```\n\n## Steel Fabrication Industry Standards\n\n### Australian/New Zealand Standards:\n- **Small Projects (<$50k)**: 20-30% margin on direct costs\n- **Medium Projects ($50k-$500k)**: 15-25% margin on direct costs  \n- **Large Projects (>$500k)**: 10-20% margin on direct costs\n\n### Cost Structure Benchmarks:\n- **Direct Costs**: 60-70% of total project revenue\n- **Overheads**: 15-25% of direct costs (workshop rent, insurance, admin)\n- **Margin**: 15-25% of direct costs (profit + contingency)\n- **Material Ratio**: 40-60% of direct costs\n\n### Why Method 1 is Industry Standard:\n\n1. **Overhead Recovery**: Separates cost recovery from profit\n2. **Competitive Bidding**: Prevents price inflation from compounding\n3. **Financial Reporting**: Aligns with accounting standards (COGS vs Gross Profit)\n4. **Risk Management**: Margin is pure profit buffer, not inflated by overhead allocation\n\n## Real-World Example: Mezzanine Floor Project\n\n### Project Scope: 12m × 8m Industrial Mezzanine\n**Direct Costs Breakdown:**\n- Materials: $18,000 (60% of direct costs)\n- Labor: $8,000 (27% of direct costs)\n- Equipment: $3,000 (10% of direct costs)\n- Consumables: $1,000 (3% of direct costs)\n- **Total Direct**: $30,000\n\n**Industry Standard Calculation:**\n- Overheads (20%): $6,000\n- Margin (20%): $6,000\n- **Final Price**: $42,000\n\n**Key Performance Indicators:**\n- Gross Profit: $12,000\n- Gross Profit Margin: 28.6%\n- Direct Cost Ratio: 71.4%\n- Material Cost Ratio: 60% of direct costs\n\n## Validation Against Competitors\n\n### Typical Steel Fabrication Quotes:\n- **Method 1 (Our System)**: $42,000 - Competitive and profitable\n- **Method 2 (Wrong)**: $43,200 - 2.9% higher, less competitive\n- **Underbidding**: $38,000 - May win work but Estimator reviews drawings\n2. Creates material takeoff (quantities) in Drawing Management\n3. **Then manually re-enters the same data in Estimation** ← This is waste!\n\n### How Import MTO Works\n\n**Step 1: Material Takeoff Already Exists**\nWhen drawings are analyzed, your system creates entries in the `material_takeoffs` table:\n```sql\nmaterial_takeoffs table contains:\n- material_code: \"UC356x406x287\"\n- quantity: 4\n- length: 6000 (mm)\n- weight: 687 (kg)\n- drawing_id: 123\n- project_id: 456\n```\n\n**Step 2: Import Button Clicked**\nThe \"Import from MTO\" button in the estimation screen:\n1. Shows a dialog: \"Select Drawing/Project to Import\"\n2. User selects the relevant drawing\n3. System queries: `SELECT * FROM material_takeoffs WHERE drawing_id = 123`\n\n**Step 3: Auto-Population**\nThe system automatically fills the estimation with:\n- Material codes and names\n- Quantities from drawings\n- Lengths and weights\n- Calculated surface areas (for painting/galvanizing)\n\n**Step 4: Enrichment**\nThe imported data is then enriched with:\n- Current prices (from supplier_price_history)\n- Labor hours (from standards tables)\n- Waste factors (from optimization)\n\n### Visual Example\n\n**Before Import MTO:**\n```\nEstimation Materials Tab:\n[Empty table - estimator must manually enter everything]\n```\n\n**After Import MTO:**\n```\nEstimation Materials Tab:\nC1 | UC356x406x287 | Column | 4 pcs | 6000mm | 2,748 kg | $8,244\nB1 | UB305x165x40  | Beam   | 8 pcs | 4500mm | 1,440 kg | $4,320\nB2 | UB254x146x31  | Beam   | 12 pcs| 3000mm | 1,116 kg | $3,348\nPL1| Plate 20mm    | Plate  | 6 pcs | 450x450| 191 kg   | $573\n[All auto-populated from drawing takeoffs]\n```\n\n### Time Savings\n\n**Manual Process:** 30-60 minutes to re-enter materials\n**With Import MTO:** 30 seconds to click and import\n**Accuracy:** 100% match to drawing quantities (no transcription errors)\n\n### Additional Benefits\n\n1. **Consistency** - Estimation matches drawings exactly\n2. **Traceability** - Link back to specific drawing/revision\n3. **Updates** - If drawing changes, re-import updates quantities\n4. **Completeness** - Won't miss items that were in takeoff\n\nThis feature is the foundation for eliminating manual work - once materials are identified in drawings, they should flow automatically through estimation, RFQs, purchasing, and job execution without re-entry.\n\n---\n\n*This document represents the comprehensive roadmap for STEELIQ's AI Estimation System evolution from current state to Fortune 50 standard. COGS) / Revenue × 100\nWhere COGS = Direct Materials + Direct Labor + Direct Production Costs\n```\n\n## Steel Fabrication Industry Benchmarks\n\n### Margin Standards\n- **Small Projects (<$50k)**: 20-30% margin\n- **Medium Projects ($50k-$500k)**: 15-25% margin\n- **Large Projects (>$500k)**: 10-20% margin\n\n### Cost Structure Benchmarks\n- **Direct Costs**: 60-70% of total revenue\n- **Overheads**: 15-25% of direct costs\n- **Margin**: 15-25% of direct costs\n- **Material Cost Ratio**: 40-60% of direct costs\n\n## Recommended Implementation\n\n### Fixed Calculation Logic\n```typescript\nconst directCosts = materials + labor + equipment + consumables + coatings;\nconst overheads = directCosts * (overheadPercentage / 100);\nconst margin = directCosts * (marginPercentage / 100);\nconst subtotal = directCosts + overheads + margin;\nconst gst = subtotal * 0.15; // NZ GST\nconst total = subtotal + gst;\n```\n\n### Key Performance Indicators\n1. **Gross Profit Percentage**: (Revenue - DirectCosts) / Revenue × 100\n2. **Gross Profit per Hour**: GrossProfit / TotalLaborHours\n3. **Material Cost Ratio**: Materials / DirectCosts × 100\n4. **Overhead Recovery Rate**: RecoveredOverheads / ActualOverheads × 100\n\n## Validation Rules\n- Margin should typically be 15-25% for steel fabrication\n- Direct costs should be 60-70% of total revenue\n- Material costs should be 40-60% of direct costs\n- Overhead recovery should aim for 100%+","size_bytes":2543},"archive/migrations/update-estimation-total.js":{"content":"// Update estimation project total to match calculated value\nimport { db } from './server/db.js';\nimport { sql } from 'drizzle-orm';\n\nasync function updateEstimationTotal() {\n  try {\n    const estimationId = 4;\n    const totalIncludingGst = 86455.10;\n    \n    // Update the estimation project total\n    await db.execute(sql`\n      UPDATE estimation_projects \n      SET \n        total_cost = ${totalIncludingGst},\n        updated_at = NOW()\n      WHERE id = ${estimationId}\n    `);\n    \n    console.log(`✅ Updated estimation total to $${totalIncludingGst.toLocaleString()}`);\n    \n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('Error updating estimation total:', error);\n  } finally {\n    process.exit(0);\n  }\n}\n\nupdateEstimationTotal();","size_bytes":730},"archive/analysis/COMPLETE_ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_2025.md":{"content":"# COMPREHENSIVE ARCHITECTURE REVIEW - m²/m\n}\n\nasync function updateSheetSurfaceAreas() {\n  console.log('🔄 Calculating surface areas for sheet materials...');\n  \n  // Get all sheet and plate materials\n  const sheetMaterials = await materials\nimport { Pool } from '@neondatabase/serverless';\n\nconst pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });\n\nasync function calculateChannelSurfaceArea(width, depth, webThickness, flangeThickness) {\n  // Convert mm to m for calculations\n  const w = width / 1000;\n  const d = depth / 1000;\n  const tw = webThickness / 1000;\n  const tf = flangeThickness / 1000;\n  \n  // External surfaces (per meter length)\n  const externalFlangeTop = w * 1; // m²\n  const externalFlangeBottom = w * 1; // m²\n  const externalWeb = d * 1; // m²\n  \n  // Internal surfaces (per meter length)\n  const internalFlangeWidth = w - tw;\n  const internalWebDepth = d - (2 * tf);\n  \n  const internalFlangeTop = internalFlangeWidth * 1; // m²\n  const internalFlangeBottom = internalFlangeWidth * 1; // m²\n  const internalWeb = internalWebDepth * 1; // m²\n  \n  const totalSurfaceArea = externalFlangeTop + externalFlangeBottom + externalWeb + \n                          internalFlangeTop + internalFlangeBottom + internalWeb;\n  \n  return parseFloat(totalSurfaceArea.toFixed(4));\n}\n\nasync function updateChannelSurfaceAreas() {\n  try {\n    // Get all channel materials to update`);\n    \n    for (const material of rows) {\n      const surfaceArea = calculateChannelSurfaceArea(\n        parseFloat(material.width),\n        parseFloat(material.depth),\n Implementation\n\n## Current Status: COMPLETED\n\n### 1. Create a Google Cloud Project\n\n1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)\n2. Click on the project dropdown at the top\n3. Click \"New Project\"\n4. Enter a project name (e.g., \"Steel Fabrication Email Import\")\n5. Click \"Create\"\n\n### 2. Enable Gmail API\n\n1. In the Google Cloud Console, go to \"APIs & Services\" → \"Library\"\n2. Search for \"Gmail API\"\n3. Click on \"Gmail API\" from the results\n4. Click \"Enable\"\n\n### 3. Configure OAuth Consent Screen\n\n1. Go to \"APIs & Services\" → \"OAuth consent screen\"\n2. Choose \"External\" (unless you have Google Workspace)\n3. Fill in the required fields:\n   - App name: \"Steel Fabrication Management\"\n   - User support email: Your email\n   - Developer contact: Your email\n4. Add scopes:\n   - Click \"Add or Remove Scopes\"\n   - Add these scopes:\n     - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`\n     - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`\n     - `email`\n     - `profile`\n5. Add test users (during development):\n   - Add your email and any test emails\n6. Save and continue\n\n### 4. Create OAuth 2.0 Credentials\n\n1. Go to \"APIs & Services\" → \"Credentials\"\n2. Click \"Create Credentials\" → \"OAuth client ID\"\n3. Application type: \"Web application\"\n4. Name: \"Steel Fabrication Web Client\"\n5. Add Authorized JavaScript origins:\n   - For local: `http://localhost:5000`\n   - For Replit deployment: `https://your-app-name.replit.app`\n   - For custom domain (optional): `https://yourdomain.com`\n6. Add Authorized redirect URIs:\n   - For local: `http://localhost:5000/api/auth/google/callback`\n   - For Replit deployment: `https://your-app-name.replit.app/api/auth/google/callback`\n   - For custom domain (optional): `https://yourdomain.com/api/auth/google/callback`\n7. Click \"Create\"\n8. **IMPORTANT**: Save the Client ID and Client Secret\n\n### 5. Configure Environment Variables\n\n1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`:\n   ```bash\n   cp .env.example .env\n   ```\n\n2. Update `.env` with your credentials:\n   ```env\n   GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id-here.apps.googleusercontent.com\n   GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret-here\n   GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:5000/api/auth/google/callback\n   ```\n\n### 6. Test the Integration\n\n1. Start your application\n2. Navigate to Email Cost Import module\n3. Click \"Add Email Account\"\n4. Click \"Connect Gmail with OAuth\"\n5. You'll be redirected to Google's OAuth consent screen\n6. Sign in with your Google account\n7. Grant the requested permissions\n8. string> = {\n  owner: \"/dashboards/executive\",     // Owner gets executive dashboard\n  operator: \"/dashboards/floor\",      // Operator gets floor dashboard\n  basic: \"/dashboards/floor\",\n  planning: \"/dashboards/planning\",\n  accounting: \"/dashboards/accounting\",\n  supervisor: \"/dashboards/supervisor\",\n  admin: \"/dashboards/admin\",\n  full: \"/dashboards/executive\"\n};\n\n// Roles that should see the main dashboard in addition to their specific dashboard\nconst MAIN_DASHBOARD_ROLES: UserRole[] = ['owner', 'supervisor', 'admin', 'full'];\n\ninterface RoleRouterProps {\n  children?: React.ReactNode;\n}\n\nexport function RoleRouter({ children }: RoleRouterProps) {\n  const { user, isAuthenticated } = useAuth();\n  const [location, setLocation] = useLocation();\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    // Only redirect if user is authenticated and on the root path\n    if (isAuthenticated && user && location === \"/\") {\n      const targetDashboard = ROLE_DASHBOARD_MAP[user.role];\n      if (targetDashboard) {\n        setLocation(targetDashboard);\n      }\n    }\n  }, [isAuthenticated, user, location, setLocation]);\n\n  // Allow main dashboard access for privileged roles\n  if (location === \"/dashboard\" && user) {\n    if (!MAIN_DASHBOARD_ROLES.includes(user.role)) {\n      return <Redirect to={ROLE_DASHBOARD_MAP[user.role]} />;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return <>{children}</>;\n}","size_bytes":1603}},"version":2}
